issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant duplicated rather than re-imported
issues.detail: In the moved Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat, a new `static final int DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT = 16` is introduced because the original was imported from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat (still in core). If the core constant ever changes, the backward-codec copy will silently drift and produce incompatible reads. Prefer importing the original constant or adding a compile-time assertion they match.

issues.description: Public API constants/methods downgraded to package-private may break consumers
issues.detail: `NAME`, `QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT`, `calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval`, and several constructors/classes were changed from `public` to package-private (or final class to package-private). Even though the formats are deprecated/moving, external code (Elasticsearch, Solr, plugins) referencing `Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME` will fail to compile. Confirm this is intentional for a major release boundary and mention in MIGRATE.txt.

issues.description: fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException but Format is still selectable by users
issues.detail: Both Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat now throw at write time. Because they remain instantiable and listed as service providers, a user invoking `new Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat()` on an index writer will fail only at flush/merge time with a cryptic message. Consider throwing at construction or in a documented `getFormatName`-style guard, and document the read-only semantics in the class Javadoc.

issues.description: Removal of numMergeWorkers/mergeExec silently changes constructor semantics
issues.detail: The constructor still accepts `numMergeWorkers` and `mergeExec` parameters and performs validation on them, but the fields are no longer stored. Callers passing a non-null executor will get past validation but the executor is silently dropped. Since writes throw, this is mostly moot, but the dead validation is misleading; consider simplifying to a single no-arg/read constructor and deleting the unused parameters.
issues.lines: constructor body around removed numMergeWorkers/mergeExec assignments

issues.description: OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues fields changed from protected to package-private
issues.detail: Fields like `dimension`, `size`, `slice`, etc. were downgraded from `protected` to package-private. The class itself is still `public abstract`, so any external subclass extending it (plugins, tests outside this package) will fail to compile or behave unexpectedly. If the intent is to lock down the hierarchy, also mark the class as effectively sealed (package-private constructor) or document the break.

issues.description: @Deprecated annotation removed when moving to backward_codecs
issues.detail: The original classes were marked `@Deprecated`; the moved versions no longer carry the annotation. While placement in `backward_codecs` signals legacy status, keeping `@Deprecated` (or `@Deprecated(forRemoval=true)`) preserves IDE/compiler warnings for any code still referencing these classes. Consider restoring it for consistency with other backward-codecs entries.

review.summary: This PR moves the Lucene99 scalar-quantized vector formats from core to backward_codecs and makes the writers throw UnsupportedOperationException, with read-time logic preserved. The mechanical move is mostly clean, but several public API surfaces are silently downgraded to package-private (NAME, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, protected fields on OffHeapQuantizedByteVectorValues), which is a binary/source break for downstream consumers like Elasticsearch/Solr. A new local copy of `DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT` introduces a drift risk against the core constant. Failing on write at flush time rather than at construction will surprise users who instantiate the format directly. Recommend documenting the API breaks in MIGRATE.txt and tightening the read-only contract earlier in the lifecycle.
